newsitem.title: ROMANIA: EBRD lends Romania $75 mln for water works.
newsitem.headline: EBRD lends Romania $75 mln for water works.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on Monday signed a $75 million loan to upgrade Romania's crumbling water utilities.

"The loan will finance priority investments in water supply and waste water in an additional 10 cities and will help improve the financial and operational performance in the water companies," an EBRD statement said.
The interest for the 15-year loan, with three years grace, is the six-month LIBOR rate plus a 100 basis points margin.

The European Commision's Phare programme, the Romanian government and municipalities are co-financing the project, worth a total $188 million, which will improve water supplies in cities across the Balkan country.
The EBRD had previously extended a $28 million loan to five Romanian townships in April 1995.
Johan Bastin, head of the EBRD's local project team, said the previous programme had helped "to create a decentralised system of funding for urban infrastructure projects".
The EBRD's long-term goal was "to create a dedicated source of funds to give greater access to non-sovereign guaranteed finance for municipalities across Romania", he said.

The EBRD has committed $310 million for Romanian infrastructure this year. That also includes $45 million to improve heating in five Romanian cities and $190 million to the recently launched MobiFon mobile telephone firm.
It has pledged to invest an extra $100 million this autumn to support privatisation of Romania's Romtelecom phone utility.
The EBRD portfolio for Romania stood at $1.05 billion in January, some 60 percent of which has gone to public sector projects.
